summary: The backlog rewrite retains an already-implemented API-diff task, reopens a settled timeout contract without reconciling the owning design records, and introduces an incorrect routing rule for open design questions.

findings.title: Already-implemented API diff is retained as a release blocker
findings.trigger: A maintainer follows the "Before the v0.5.0 release" checklist and implements the O-15 entry.
findings.consequence: The maintainer adds duplicate release tooling or a dependency even though pull requests already receive a javap API-surface diff and migration-guide gate, so the checklist misstates the remaining release work.
findings.evidence: BACKLOG.md:27-29 requests a new cross-version API surface diff. scripts/check-api-surface.py:223-224 and scripts/check-api-surface.py:329-342 already diff two compiled class trees and report additions and removals, and .github/workflows/ci.yml:130-139 runs that check for pull requests. design/proposal/P0022-documentation-maintenance.md:40-41 explicitly says historical O-15 is already implemented and must not be opened again.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove O-15 from the pre-release backlog. If a release-tag-to-release-tag comparison remains desirable, rewrite the entry to identify that specific uncovered gap and reconcile P0022 rather than requesting the existing pull-request diff.

findings.title: Pure-timeout entry conflicts with the settled contract
findings.trigger: A maintainer uses the 1.0.0 breaking-change batch to decide whether a pure-timeout batch should return an aggregate failedTaskResult.
findings.consequence: Current sources give opposing directions for the same public contract, leaving maintainers unable to tell whether 1.0.0 should preserve the documented behavior or make a breaking change.
findings.evidence: BACKLOG.md:15-19 presents O-13 as undecided. core/src/main/java/io/github/monadrome/parallelinscope/TaskBatchResult.java:168-181 already specifies and implements an empty result for deadline-or-cancellation-only batches, and docs/en/testing/task-batch-result-report-test-design.md:28-29 repeats that contract. design/decision-log.md:558 and design/proposal/P0022-documentation-maintenance.md:36-41 say to keep the current semantics and treat O-13 as teaching work, with any aggregate-cancellation change requiring separate evaluation.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove O-13 from the breaking-API batch and retain the documentation work in P0022. If reopening the contract is intentional, record the new rationale and update the decision log and P0022 in the same change.

findings.title: Open questions are routed to the closed-decision log
findings.trigger: A maintainer with an unresolved design choice follows the new BACKLOG routing guidance.
findings.consequence: The choice can be recorded as a conclusion in the decision log instead of entering the proposal lifecycle, bypassing the proposal route and review expected for unresolved design work.
findings.evidence: BACKLOG.md:3-6 says open design questions live in design/decision-log.md and design/proposal/. design/AGENTS.md:10-17 assigns unresolved work to tracked proposals and rejected or superseded conclusions to the decision log; design/AGENTS.md:45-48 likewise makes a conclusion and rejection reason prerequisites for decision-log entries. BACKLOG.md:15-19 itself demonstrates the contradiction by retaining an open decision.
findings.suggestedFix: Route open design questions only to design/proposal/ and reserve design/decision-log.md for rejected, superseded, or otherwise concluded directions; keep BACKLOG limited to scheduled release actions.
